original_value: AbstractBackgroundMachine learning can assist with multiple tasks during systematic reviews to facilitate the rapid retrieval of relevant references during screening and to identify and extract information relevant to the study characteristics, which include the PICO elements of patient/population, intervention, comparator, and outcomes. The latter requires techniques for identifying and categorising fragments of text, known as named entity recognition.MethodsA publicly available corpus of PICO annotations on biomedical abstracts is used to train a named entity recognition model, which is implemented as a recurrent neural network. This model is then applied to a separate collection of abstracts for references from systematic reviews within biomedical and health domains. The occurrences of words tagged in the context of specific PICO contexts are used as additional features for a relevancy classification model. Simulations of the machine learning-assisted screening are used to evaluate the work saved by the relevancy model with and without the PICO features. Chi-squared and statistical significance of positive predicted values are used to identify words that are more indicative of relevancy within PICO contexts.ResultsInclusion of PICO features improves the performance metric on 15 of the 20 collections, with substantial gains on certain systematic reviews. Examples of words whose PICO context are more precise can explain this increase.ConclusionsWords within PICO tagged segments in abstracts are predictive features for determining inclusion. Combining PICO annotation model into the relevancy classification pipeline is a promising approach. The annotations may be useful on their own to aid users in pinpointing necessary information for data extraction, or to facilitate semantic search.

The latter task requires methods that identify and categorize text fragments, known as named entity recognition.MethodsA publicly available corpus of PICO annotations on biomedical abstracts is used to train a named entity recognition model implemented as a recurrent neural network. The model is then applied to a separate set of abstracts from systematic review references in biomedical and health domains. Words tagged in specific PICO contexts are used as additional features for a relevancy classification model. Simulations of machine learning-assisted screening assess the work saved by the relevancy model with and without PICO features. Chi-squared tests and statistical significance of positive predicted values are used to find words that better indicate relevancy within PICO contexts.ResultsAdding PICO features improves the performance metric on 15 of the 20 collections, with substantial gains in some systematic reviews. Examples of words with more precise PICO contexts help explain this increase.ConclusionsWords in PICO-tagged abstract segments are predictive features for determining inclusion. Integrating the PICO annotation model into the relevancy classification pipeline is a promising approach. The annotations may also be useful on their own to help users pinpoint needed information for data extraction or to support semantic search.
